messages:
maria: Heads-up — us-west p4p pool hit sustained GPU saturation around 03:20 UTC, queues backed up. I'm thinking we should move from RPS/RPM-based admission to token-based admission (TPM) so rate limits map directly to capacity. Anyone object?
kevin: +1 on token-based. We already measure per-request token usage per model, so converting should be doable. main questions: 1) how to map GPU capacity -> token throughput, 2) how to handle bursts, 3) dedicated vs shared pools.
asha: Important: for Dedicated customers we can't silently throttle to shared fairness levels. Need a way to honor reserved capacity and only apply token admission to best-effort tiers.
devops-bot: [alert] p4p-pool-us-west: gpu_util=97% for 6m, queued_requests=312, avg_seq_len=512 tokens, dominant_model=redwood-7B-q4_0 (70%).
leo: Implementation-wise we need a per-pool token budget metric that the gateway checks before enqueueing. Rough calc idea: pool_tokens_per_min = sum(gpu_token_throughput_per_min) * safety_margin. We can derive gpu_token_throughput from measured tokens/sec at target p99 latency per model.
jin: For admission control I recommend a token-bucket style approach per pool and per-tenant. Refill rate = pool_tokens_per_min / 60 (tokens/sec). Bucket size = burst_window_seconds * refill_rate. That gives controlled bursts without unbounded queueing. Example: 
```
# example numbers
gpu_tokens_per_min = 600k  # measured on A100 for mixed workloads
gpus = 8
pool_tokens_per_min = gpu_tokens_per_min * gpus * 0.85  # 15% headroom
// tenant_share = 0.2 -> tenant_tpm = pool_tokens_per_min * 0.2
```
kevin: Nice. We'll need model-specific multipliers; e.g., chat-completions average tokens_out/token_in ratio increases token usage. Also remember system prompt and tool-calls contribute tokens.
asha: Also surface cost signals: tokens_allowed should be tied to billing units for hosted customers, and show projected spend if they hit their limit. For committed dedicated customers, map their reserved GPUs -> guaranteed token budget.
sre-oncall: Queue growth is causing memory pressure on the gateway pods (OOM risk). If tokens queued exceed threshold we should either start shedding (429) or fallback to cheaper model variants automatically. We had a near-OOM last week when a two-hour burst hit.
leo: Fallback policy idea: route to quantized variant (e.g., redwood-7B-q5 -> q4) or a lower-context model. Prefer gradual degradation: 1) allow token bursts up to bucket, 2) if queue still rising, switch low-priority traffic to fallback, 3) if still saturated, reject.
jin: Telemetry we need: tokens_served_total, tokens_queued, token_refill_rate, tokens_available_pool, tokens_available_tenant, avg_tokens_per_request_by_model. Those let autoscaler and routing make decisions.
kevin: Rollout plan: prototype admission adapter in request-gateway, run canary in staging, then us-west best-effort pool at 5% traffic for 24h. Monitor p99 latency, queued_tokens, and OOM signals. If stable, increase to 25% then full.
maria: Action items: kevin -> prototype gateway adapter + metrics (start today). jin -> implement token-bucket admission logic (PR draft by EOD). leo -> dashboard: tokens_available, tokens_queued, per-model avg_tokens (grafana panels). asha -> define mapping for dedicated contracts to token budgets. sre-oncall -> add alerting thresholds to avoid OOMs. I'll coordinate the canary window. :thumbsup:
kevin: one more: we should store a per-model token-cost profile and recalc hourly using a sliding window, that avoids stale multipliers when customers change prompts.
asha: Agreed. Also add a policy flag so sales can opt-in/opt-out tenants from token throttling until legal sign-off.
leo: I added a small script to compute gpu_tokens_per_min from perf-tests. Will push to infra/test-utils repo and wire to the canonical metric.
jin: I'll include tests that simulate bursts and ensure the bucket drains at expected rate. Also will add a dry-run mode that logs admissions without blocking.
sre-oncall: I'll add an emergency bypass that moves low-priority traffic off the pool when host memory > 80% to avoid cascading failures.
maria: Great — keep updates in this thread. If anyone is blocked ping me or drop a short note in #eng-oncall.
